qualitative_or_quantitative_description.value: Cr23C6 carbides in granular or banded shapes at austenite grain boundaries may lead to inter-granular cracking along coarsening carbides at the grain boundary; the appearance of Cr23C6 carbide particles at the grain boundary is the main reason for the poor ductility and high strain hardening rate of as-cast and annealed 9Cr strips.

comparison_metric.value: Among the annealed strips, the 9Cr strip has the highest ultimate tensile strength (994 ± 21 MPa) but the lowest total elongation (22.8 ± 4 %). The formation of Cr23C6 carbides causes the lowest ductility of the as-cast and annealed 9Cr strips.

unmapped_findings: Increment of yield strength after annealing (annealed 9Cr minus as-cast 9Cr) is +65 MPa, and increment of total elongation after annealing is +2.5 % (Table 2).

The addition of 9 wt.% Cr improves the solid solubility of C and inhibits the precipitation of κ-carbides, while the precipitation of Cr23C6 in the 9Cr sample reduces the formation of dislocations, leading to fewer dislocations in the austenite of the 9Cr strip than of the 6Cr strip.
The appearance of Cr23C6 carbide particles at the grain boundary is the main reason for the poor ductility and high strain hardening rate of as-cast and annealed 9Cr strips.

Compared with as-cast strips, the strain hardening rate of all annealed strips except the 9Cr strip clearly decreases (i.e., the annealed 9Cr strain hardening rate does not clearly decrease); the strain hardening rate of annealed strips increases with increasing Cr content.

The grain boundaries and dendritic structure of the annealed 0Cr strip are clearly observed by SEM, while the grain boundary could not be observed in the Cr-containing strips (including 9Cr) under the same conditions, indicating that Cr addition improves the corrosion resistance of the steel strips.
As-cast 6Cr and 9Cr ferrite shows a DO3 superlattice (nano-scale DO3 phases) that is absent in the as-cast 0Cr and 3Cr ferrite (Fig. 5c,d).
